correctness.rationale: For every p,q>=1 with ordinary unweighted adjacency, the double-star bipartite off-diagonal block has rank two and F(s)=s^2-(p+q+1)s+pq with two distinct positive roots mu_±. This gives four simple nonzero eigenvalues and one zero eigenspace of dimension p+q-2, whose projector is Q_p ⊕ Q_q on the leaf blocks. For positive-energy squared eigenvector profiles w_±, the exact average mixing is E0∘E0+2w_+w_+^T+2w_-w_-^T. The leaf Schur-squares Q_s∘Q_s have constant eigenvalue (s-1)/s and transverse eigenvalue (s-2)/s, hence ranks f(1)=0, f(2)=1 and f(s>=3)=s. Modulo their ranges, the two profile vectors have independent hub projections exactly for p≠q because determinant (p-q)/(4Delta); singleton leaves add a residual coordinate without losing the two-profile rank. For p=q one hub relation remains, and at p=q=1 the profiles span a two-dimensional range. This proves the four nullity cases and the iff full-rank frontier. The listed pair-difference and singleton-side three-coordinate vectors satisfy every Schur-square kernel condition and match the computed dimension; hence form complete bases. Independent 225-case eigenspace/matrix enumeration and symbolic determinant/orthogonality checks agree, but the all-positive-integer assertion rests on this proof rather than finite sampling.

evidence: Coutinho et al. arXiv:2208.08971 provide an exact algorithm for entries of average mixing on arbitrary integral adjacency matrices, not a symbolic sharp p,q-dependent nullspace theorem.
Mohan et al. arXiv:2608.20739, accessible abstract only, studies the trace of Laplacian average mixing and an unbalanced double-star ordering, not the rank of the adjacency average-mixing matrix.
Fan and Godsil arXiv:1206.0082 is specific to the identical double-star adjacency graph but studies phase-sensitive quantum state transfer and strongly cospectral vertices, not the Cesaro rank.
broader_coverage.reasoning: An algorithm which computes the matrix for each fixed pair can in principle be used to rediscover the result, but does not state or immediately imply the uniform classification. Laplacian and adjacency Hamiltonians have different projectors on irregular double stars, and trace does not determine kernel. A full-text comparison to Mohan et al. was not possible, so any incidental stronger statement is a residual priority risk rather than a claimed disproof.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge novelty for the complete two-parameter, ordinary-adjacency, double-star Cesaro average-mixing nullity, explicit full kernel bases, and sharp positive-definite boundary. Primary sources provide the Schur-square spectral identity, abstract rank/commutant bounds, individual-graph exact computation, and double-star state-transfer results but do not state or imply the parameter-uniform full-kernel classification. A separately identified recent Laplacian paper is abstract-only and left as a residual risk. Search absence is not treated as proof of novelty.
residual_risks: The complete Mohan–Tamon–Xu–Zhan arXiv:2608.20739 paper could not be lawfully read; the abstract specifies Laplacian trace rather than adjacency rank, but incidental matching content cannot be excluded. Authorized institutional access reported vpn_disconnected.

General commutant/equitable-partition or zero-mode formulas may have been specialized to the double star under alternative names (bistar, diameter-three tree), including sources not indexed by the searches.

value.rationale: The mean mixing matrix of the continuous-time adjacency quantum walk is a natural long-time transport invariant. Double stars are a standard nontrivial diameter-three family with arbitrarily large zero adjacency eigenspaces and prior state-transfer interest. The theorem gives the full kernel and a sharp positive-definiteness classification for every p,q≥1, distinguishing equal-arm symmetry, two-leaf twins, and singleton-leaf three-coordinate constraints. It provides structural information not determined by trace/laziness, pairwise strong cospectrality, or per-instance computations. Its scope is precisely the unweighted adjacency family; no universal tree theorem, finite-time mixing rate, or perturbative stability is claimed.
